PSYC 500: This course will familiarize students with the standards of ethical conduct related to research and practice in psychology and counseling.
PSYC 501: This course will familiarize students with the need for sensitivity to individual and group differences associated with culture and ethnicity.
PSYC 502: An examination of social psychological applications to areas such as health, law, interpersonal relations, environment, politics, and other social issues.
PSYC 509: This course is designed to provide an in-depth examination of addiction, encompassing its conceptualization and various theoretical frameworks for understanding its etiology and persistence.
PSYC 510: The course covers human development across the life span.
PSYC 514: This course focuses on the theoretical, conceptual, programmatic, and empirical issues currently in preventive psychology.
PSYC 515: This course examines wellness maintenance, early detection, and the impact of health care on individuals and the community.
PSYC 516: This course will familiarize students with health issues in the context of child development and family systems.
PSYC 517: A broad spectrum view of psychopathology including biological, social, cognitive, psychological, and neuropsychological approaches, is emphasized, with an applied focus.
PSYC 519: An advanced level of psychotherapies and applications in diverse settings.
PSYC 520: This course is intended to provide students in the Applied Psychology Clinical program with a basis for understanding psychological research methodologies.
PSYC 521: The nature, computation, computer analysis, interpretation, and APA-style write-up will be discussed for a number of statistical tests.
PSYC 524: This course focuses on biological determinants of behavior, including evolution, hormones, sensory systems, internal states, reproduction, emotions, learning, and memory.
PSYC 525: This course will explore social, cognitive, civil and criminal issues related to forensic psychology.
PSYC 530: Supervised research in psychology for degree candidates.
PSYC 535: Analysis of determinants of behavior and behavioral ecology.
PSYC 571: Administration, analysis, and interpretation of psychological evaluation methods will be reviewed.
PSYC 572: This course will review the biological bases of behavior, emphasizing brain-behavioral relationships and assessment of these relationships.
PSYC 594: Supervised student activities on research projects identified on an individual or small group basis.
PSYC 596: Creative projects, including nonthesis research, that are supervised on an individual basis and which fall outside the scope of formal courses.
PSYC 597: Formal courses given on a topical or special interest subject which may be offered infrequently; several different topics may be taught in one year or semester.
PSYC 818: In this course students will begin to practice eliciting information from classmates, or volunteer undergraduate students, simulating individuals presenting with a variety of issues, use that information to make an appropriate diagnosis, and work with their mock client to set goals and develop a concrete plan to achieve those goals.
PSYC 840: This course covers applications of empirically-supported psychotherapeutic theories and techniques to a group setting.
PSYC 841: This course will provide a foundation for understanding couple and family systems theories, assessments, and interventions.
PSYC 843: This course covers the etiology, symptoms, diagnosis, and treatment of trauma-related dysfunction, particularly post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), acute stress disorder (ASD), and common comorbid conditions.
PSYC 844: This course covers issues concerning the diagnosis and treatment of complex trauma-related dysfunction, particularly post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), Dissociative Disorders, and treating special populations issues.
PSYC 845: This course will provide students foundational knowledge about crisis intervention and disaster interventions.
PSYC 895A: This course will give students their first experience of working with clients in a psychological setting.
PSYC 895B: This course is designed to aid meeting standards for Pennsylvania mental health counselor licensure, specifically the LPC (Licensed Professional Counselor).
